# Repository overview

Pipa is a Node.js command-line application with Socket and Managed profile modes. Socket Mode connects Slack to one persistent private `opencode serve` process, or to an explicitly configured existing server. Managed mode owns one persistent `opencode serve` child without connecting to Slack. Configuration and Socket Mode session IDs are stored under `~/.pipa`.

This shared-checkout candidate combines native v1/v2 migration work with main's model picker and Slack lifecycle behavior. The current native v2 target to qualify is **2.2.5**, alongside historical v2 **2.0.29** and v1 pins **1.18.35 / 1.19.0**. The SDK remains `@opencode/client@2.0.29` until qualified. This overview describes the integration contract, not evidence that tests, compatibility, migration, or release gates have passed.

## Request flow

1. `bin/pipa.mjs` handles `pipa init` or `pipa start`, loads the profile, and selects Socket or Managed mode.
2. During initialization, `src/app.mjs` validates OpenCode and Slack credentials, reports missing capabilities without blocking, then `src/state.mjs` saves the configuration and generated Slack manifest under `~/.pipa`. The internal `src/slack-permissions.mjs` owns the private capability map and notice formatting; `app.mjs` calls its single exported helper at init/start. Bot grants come first from the direct `auth.test` response's `x-oauth-scopes` header, then a raw-body metadata fallback; unknown grants remain silent. The generated manifest is the default experience, not the runtime minimum. See the [complete permission audit](../README.md#slack-permissions), including unused generated user grants. Current status access accepts `chat:write` or the explicitly transitional `assistant:write`; missing the latter alone does not establish status loss.
3. During Socket Mode startup, `src/app.mjs` checks that `PIPA_OPENCODE_ATTACH_URL` or one owned OpenCode server on loopback port `0` can serve the configured workspace, then creates the Slack connection, restores previously subscribed Slack threads from `~/.pipa/sessions.json`, reconciles `~/.pipa/routines.json`, and starts the local 30-second routine scheduler. Ordinary v1/v2 detection, listening/readiness and Slack initialization have no default overall startup limit or migration-status gate; OpenCode owns schema/data upgrades, never Pipa. Explicit harness deadlines remain supported; per-request safety timeouts retry, while terminal auth/protocol/wrong-workspace errors fail. Ctrl+C cancels startup and stops owned children, leaving attached servers alive. During Managed startup, `src/opencode.mjs` starts one `opencode serve` child with the profile's working directory, hostname, and port; Managed mode does not execute routines. Detached background restart and shutdown deadlines are unchanged.
4. An authorized mention or subscribed-thread reply, including attachments, is routed to its mapped session. With `mentionOnly` enabled, unmentioned subscribed-thread replies are ignored. V2 serializes prompt admission per Slack thread, then lets native OpenCode steering and background execution continue; it does not interrupt the session for each follow-up. V1 retains interrupt-and-replace behavior. Different threads run independently.
   All turns pass only the current request, attachments/full links, and Slack channel/thread identity; prompt assembly never fetches or injects earlier messages, including for new or replacement sessions. Agents receive a short instruction to explicitly read the thread through their Slack tools if earlier context is needed. Existing OpenCode history is left intact. Config reads remain cancellable without their own deadlines; cancellation and revoked access still prevent submission.
5. `src/opencode.mjs` checks incoming attachment metadata and downloaded bytes against 10 MiB per file and selects the native adapter. Session mappings are saved before admission. V1 uses prompt system instructions. V2 keeps stable Slack context in native session instructions, sends exact-text prompts with native IDs, and forwards live native events for completed assistant responses. Successful admission is not vetoed by comparing echoed prompt text. Native session moves preserve the mapping and response follower; the configured directory is a starting location, not session confinement. The follower stays attached after the first reply, but does not recover replies missed during a disconnect or restart. Startup restores Slack subscriptions and conversation mappings without reattaching old background work; a new message reattaches its thread. Files retain path, type, identity and size checks; v2's private artifact directory stays in the starting location across moves and background resumptions. Incoming background attachments are admitted as data URIs so deleting local staging cannot break deferred native reads.
6. `src/app.mjs` saves the session ID and posts naturally short text once. Generated files travel with their concise summary in one Chat SDK post; a failed file post receives one text-only retry. Longer inline fallback is split at readable boundaries while preserving fenced code. Existing message reactions still report receipt, success, and failure.
7. Due routines call the same executor with a fresh session, exact saved prompt, configured working directory, and saved Slack channel or thread. After delivery, Pipa binds and subscribes the result thread to that OpenCode session so replies continue it. The scheduler permits different routines to overlap but never overlaps one routine with itself. Every dispatch, interaction, response, and final delivery reloads the relevant authorization. Edits affect future work; deactivation and deletion abort active work. Destination revocation blocks a new run or result delivery at the next authorization check. Shutdown aborts active work and suppresses stale delivery.
8. After full readiness, the CLI watches generation-scoped restart requests. The running Pipa arms a detached worker before cooperative shutdown, awaits cleanup and ownership-aware lock release, and awaits the worker handoff before exiting naturally. The worker waits for the old lock and process, starts the absolute packaged CLI detached, and records success only after replacement readiness IPC. Managed replacements must pass a bounded workspace health check; startup failure stops their owned child and releases the lock before reporting failure. Ordinary Managed starts remain running if health is unavailable, but cannot accept restart requests. Existing Slack authorization is unchanged.

- `src/models.mjs`: Registers one private native Slack model picker for both the normalized name command (`Chopper` -> `/chopper model`) and `/pipa model`. A loading window opens before discovery, then becomes a native external select. Routine create/preview snapshots the default into an optional immutable record field, and routine dispatch uses only that explicit snapshot. Save acknowledges by closing promptly; tracked background work validates and persists the choice and delivers a private result to the opening channel. Duplicate submissions do not duplicate writes. Windows termination uses `taskkill` to stop descendants.
- `src/opencode-v1.mjs`: Owns native v1 session resolution, prompt/status/message reconciliation, event-driven questions and permissions, and server cancellation. Request connection/body-read failures do not stop the server; actual owned-process exit and explicit shutdown still do.
- `src/opencode-v2.mjs`: Uses pinned `@opencode/client@2.0.29` for native session admission and live event following. Slack response observers outlive individual requests and receive later background completions. No response-history resync, delivery replay, custom attribution guard, temporary instruction cleanup, recovery journal, or installation-wide blocked flag is used. Reconnect rechecks session identity and pending interactions, not past responses or a frozen directory. Interaction reconciliation discovers native descendants and reads session-scoped forms/permissions across moves. Interaction network work is queued per observer so it cannot block other sessions' response events. Both adapters expose `interaction.submit(decision)` and `interaction.settled`; native refusal leaves controls editable. The adapter waits for the location change before resubmitting that definitely rejected payload once with the same message ID. ## Product Contract

### Summary

Support OpenCode v1 and v2 in one Pipa release, including owned and attached runtimes. Keep Slack, routines, restart, and delivery behavior shared; verify both adapters through the same feature contract and real-runtime harness.

### Problem Frame

Pipa currently requires OpenCode v1 during initialization and uses v1 HTTP payloads throughout execution. An OpenCode v2 upgrade breaks the unchanged executor. Requiring users to choose a matching Pipa release would move compatibility work onto them. The protocol spike demonstrated useful common ACP support but a v1 question gap and a different attached-server connection model; native HTTP adapters preserve the existing feature surface.

### Requirements

**Runtime and continuity**

- R1. One Pipa package automatically selects the v1 or v2 HTTP adapter from authenticated runtime identity and validated contracts in Socket-owned, Managed, and attached modes. Unsupported/missing runtimes fail with actionable guidance before Socket intake; no user adapter flag, global OpenCode replacement, or forced v1-to-v2 upgrade is introduced.
- R2. Previously persisted Slack thread mappings resume migrated sessions with history intact; failed migration must not silently create replacement sessions.
- R3. An owned server remains private and process-owned; an attached server is checked but never started, restarted, or killed by Pipa.
- R4. New messages supersede active same-thread work without stale output, state writes, or success reactions; other threads remain independent.

**Interactions and delivery**

- R5. Native v1 questions/permissions and v2 question forms/permissions appear in the correct Slack thread, including linked child requests, with existing responder authorization. Preserve the existing choice, multiselect, custom-answer, approval, and dismissal experience.
- R6. Reconnection or location reload reconciles pending controls and makes stale responses inert.
- R7. Slack context, routine/restart guidance, and artifact instructions reach the intended agent turn without leaking into another thread or a later turn.
- R8. Pipa accepts incoming files up to 10 MiB (10,485,760 bytes) each and rejects larger files with a clear message before prompt admission. Enforce the limit against both supplied size metadata and downloaded bytes; preserve the other incoming attachment behavior. User revision on 2026-10-15 supersedes the earlier 20 MiB decision after native boundary failure.
- R9. Preserve artifact containment, symlink and identity checks, 10-file/100 MB response limits, temporary-file cleanup, concise delivery, and text-only upload fallback.

**Routines and follow-up foundation**

- R10. Routines retain exact saved prompts, destination/responder authorization checks, overlap prevention, cancellation, and result-thread continuation.
- R11. Qualify native v2 delegated execution, result return, and child approvals against Pipa's existing delegation/delivery behavior. Preserve the current Slack experience; do not add a new acknowledgement, late-result notification, or background-job interface as part of the migration.
- R12. Verify connected-model discovery and v2 native live switching on the existing session, including variants/default semantics and history preservation. V1 must not claim next-provider-step switching. The Slack model picker is now pre-existing behavior to preserve; additional picker/help UI and v1 capability expansion remain outside this migration.
- R13. Keep supported existing OpenCode configuration and file-based definitions initially; identify required plugins that need a separate v2 implementation.
- R14. Verify the common feature contract against both adapters and the qualified real-runtime matrix, including actual scheduler dispatch and detached Socket/Managed restart. Record missing environments, capabilities, or responders as blocked coverage, never passed.

### Key Decisions

- **Runtime compatibility before model UI** (session-settled: user-approved — chosen over building the picker first: verify the runtime contract before depending on it). Governs R1, R12.
- **Session-bound selection** (session-settled: user-directed — chosen over a conversation picker: use the conversation the user is already in). Governs R12.
- **Runtime port before Slack picker/help UI** (session-settled: user-approved — chosen over bundling UI into the migration: verify the underlying runtime first). Governs R12.
- **10 MiB incoming files** (session-settled: user-approved — user revision on 2026-10-15 supersedes the earlier 20 MiB choice after its native boundary failure). Governs R8. R9 retains the existing outgoing artifact limits.
- **Portable live-test configuration** (session-settled: user-directed — chosen over documenting one operator's Slack setup: contributors must supply their own credentials and destinations). Support either a separate test app or controlled reuse of an existing app through private configuration. Governs R14.
- **One release, two internal HTTP adapters** (session-settled: user-approved — chosen over ACP-only or separate Pipa releases: preserve current features and make runtime selection transparent). Governs R1, R14. This replaces the earlier v2-only decision.

### Acceptance Examples

- AE1. **Covers R2:** Given an existing thread and migrated session, a follow-up recalls prior context and retains the session ID.
- AE2. **Covers R4:** Given two active threads, a newer message in one interrupts only that thread; only the latest turn delivers a result there.
- AE3. **Covers R5, R6:** Given a child permission request and a disconnected client, reconnect restores one authorized Slack control; an externally settled request cannot be answered again.
- AE4. **Covers R10:** Given a routine result, a reply continues the result session; revoking its destination before delivery prevents delivery.
- AE5. **Covers R12:** Native v2 switching affects subsequent provider turns and preserves history without a Pipa restart; the v1 adapter does not advertise that capability.
- AE6. **Covers R1, R14:** An unchanged Pipa profile starts against either supported generation and routes a turn through the detected adapter; attaching to v2 works even when the local executable is v1.

### Scope Boundaries

Port the protocol boundary and qualify the existing product behaviors. Add only two version-specific runtime files and the reusable test infrastructure they require. Operator-specific credentials, app/channel IDs, and plugin inventories remain private inputs.

#### Deferred to Follow-Up Work

- Additional model/help UI, message shortcut, and help app action. The original Slack picker deferral is historical: the implemented picker and existing model commands are baseline behavior, not deferred migration deliverables.
- Wholesale conversion of supported v1 configuration to native v2 syntax.
- Adoption of the shared user service as Pipa's default process model.
- Durable replay infrastructure or an embedded OpenCode server solely to enable event persistence.
- New Slack background-work UX, automatic acknowledgement/follow-up policies, and user-facing background controls. R11 is compatibility qualification, not a new product flow.
- ACP adoption, forked Pipa releases, a generic transport/plugin framework, automatic OpenCode installation, custom restoration of remembered grants, and new generic-form UI.

### Execution-Time Qualification

- Current native v2 qualification target is 2.2.5; 2.0.29 remains a historical comparison pin alongside v1 pins 1.18.35 and 1.19.0. The v2 client remains pinned to 2.0.29. Pin inclusion is not completed release qualification. Establish a supported minimum per major from passing production-harness cells and check required contracts at startup; do not promise every historical/future release or reject newer patches solely for not matching an exact binary pin.
- **Deferred to operator trial — plugin availability:** Inventory required plugins in a private test profile; block cutover if a required v1 plugin has no working v2 port. Do not publish that profile's secrets or personal configuration.
- **Deferred to live validation — credentials and operator handoff:** Supply the chosen app, channel, sender, and responder through private environment/profile configuration. If reusing an app, confirm its existing consumer is stopped before candidate startup. Local implementation can proceed before this handoff; checked-in plans and examples contain no operator-specific channel or app IDs.

## Definition of Done

- One installed Pipa package automatically selects the validated native v1/v2 adapter without a global binary replacement or user version-routing flag.
- R8 is enforced in both incoming size checks, documented as 10 MiB, and verified at the exact byte boundary without reducing outgoing artifact limits.
- U1–U9 have their specified evidence; the shared harness, pinned matrix, actual migration/rollback, and live gates are completed before release qualification or live cutover.
- The main feature matrix has no unreported failures or blocked mandatory rows. Routines and Socket/Managed restart have real-runtime evidence in addition to deterministic tests.
- Existing thread continuity, authorizations, same-thread supersession, cross-thread independence, routine exactness, restart ownership, and artifact safety remain demonstrable.
- Model discovery/switching are qualified for the follow-up UI, including reset and variant semantics.
- V1 wire paths stay confined to the v1 adapter/fixtures; no v1 request is sent through the v2 adapter, and shared scheduler/Slack delivery logic has no version branch.
- Abandoned trial code and temporary data are removed; no credentials, personal configuration, or local Pipa state enter the repository.
- User-facing runtime documentation matches the qualified release and settled compatibility policy.

## Recommendation

Use one Pipa package with a shared executor contract and automatic selection of v1/v2 HTTP adapters. Retain the existing v1 integration and port only the v2 protocol boundary. Keep Slack behavior, routines, delivery checks, and restart orchestration shared.

ACP is a promising common interface, but the tested v1 releases do not provide the question tool over ACP. Moving every version to ACP would regress a current Pipa feature or require an additional bridge. V2's ACP command also rejects an explicit existing-server attachment flag; a pure ACP switch does not preserve Pipa's current attached-server connection model.

This is a recommendation from a compatibility spike, not approval to change the migration plan's product scope or proof that the final integration is ready to deploy.

## Tradeoffs

- **ACP everywhere:** One protocol client for basic owned execution; measured v1 question gap and existing-server attachment differences prevent claiming feature parity. Patching around them would reintroduce version-specific behavior and potentially multiple transports.
- **Two HTTP adapters inside one Pipa release:** Preserve the existing v1 features and current server ownership/attachment model. Port v2's admission, completion, forms, and permission differences behind the same executor interface. Compatibility tests must run against both adapters.
- **Separate Pipa releases/branches:** Does not improve the protocol gaps and makes users choose a matching package. There is no evidence from this spike that duplicating the application is necessary.
- **V2-only:** Technically viable through either v2 HTTP or ACP, but requires users to upgrade their installed runtime. It does not satisfy version-transparent support for existing v1 users.

The product promise should describe supported capabilities and automatic connection selection, not an unconditional guarantee for every historical or future OpenCode release. Qualify the supported runtime range and report incompatible capabilities before accepting work.

The original cancellation/recovery claims were too strong. Eight focused cases

### Instruction mutation ordering and uncertainty

The private journal now records instruction state (`absent`, `putting`,
`present`) independently of prompt admission. `putting` is persisted before PUT.
The PUT uses its own bounded signal, not the turn's cancellation signal. If its
success reply arrives, Pipa records `present` before proceeding; cancellation
then orders DELETE after that acknowledged write. A lost reply or timeout keeps
`putting` durable, blocks intake, and does not issue a speculative DELETE.

An acknowledged DELETE or a currently absent entry cannot prove that a prior
PUT will not commit later. Startup therefore also blocks on `putting` (and on
legacy `prepared` records lacking instruction-state evidence). Automatically
resolving that uncertainty requires native mutation fencing or independently
verified settlement/termination of the original writer. No blind journal
deletion or instruction-absence heuristic is used. The SIGKILL test distinguishes
uncertain PUTs, which retain the record and block, from acknowledged instruction
registration, whose owned context can be removed before intake without replay.

### Active cancellation is a native capability blocker

Pinned `@opencode/protocol@2.0.29` declares `session.interrupt` with only a
session ID and optional `resume`; the pinned generated SDK has the same inputs.
There is no expected input ID, sequence, revision, or compare-and-interrupt
predicate. `session.inbox.cancel` does identify one pending input, but explicitly
cannot cancel an already delivered input. A GET followed by session-wide
interrupt cannot exclude a foreign admission between those operations.

Pipa no longer calls v2 `session.interrupt` during cleanup. Known pending Pipa
inputs remain cancellable by ID, including when a foreign input is queued or a
cancellation reply is lost. Reconciliation reads inbox before messages so native
atomic inbox-to-message promotion cannot disappear between those snapshots;
this ordering never authorizes a session-wide interrupt. If an owned input is already promoted and has no
terminal idle projection, local cancellation suppresses delivery, removes only
acknowledged owned context, retains unsettled ownership and blocks further
intake. It does **not** promise to stop the active engine execution. Reconciliation
can clear settled owned work once its authoritative terminal projection exists;
the blocked live executor does not silently reopen intake. A regression inserts
foreign work immediately after cleanup's snapshot and verifies zero interrupts.
This is a genuine unresolved R4/KTD3/KTD11 compatibility boundary, not an atomicity
fix achieved by another read.

### Final attribution and reservations

The live watcher remains active through cleanup. Foreign input observed by the
final projection or watcher suppresses success even when the owned input already
has a successful idle marker. If owned work is settled and its context removal
is acknowledged, its journal record can be cleared while the attribution error
still prevents delivery; this alone does not permanently block the executor.
This does not claim a native exclusive-writer lease or a linearizable boundary
against independent admissions after the last observable check.

The shared facade reserves an existing session before downloads, callbacks, or
artifact allocation and retains the reservation through file cleanup. Duplicate
same-session callers fail before those effects; distinct sessions remain
independent. A reservation that has not resolved its session only aborts local
work, preserving the prior server-cancellation boundary.

### Bounded disconnected recovery

Authoritative reads now have a bounded recovery window after transport failure
(10 seconds by default), bounded individual HTTP requests (5 seconds), and a
fresh bounded authenticated confirmation read/projection (1 second) before one
`onFatal` notification. Persistent refusal terminates local execution and retains
uncertain ownership. Attached engine processes are never killed by this adapter.
Repeated uncertain admission replies are also bounded and reuse the same input
ID; a healthy authoritative read does not falsely declare the server dead.
Stream reconnection is bounded before initial subscription readiness, while
post-subscription stream loss can reconcile through healthy projections.

These are connection/mutation deadlines, not deadlines on healthy agent work.
Tests cover brief projection and stream outages recovering without `onFatal`,
healthy work continuing beyond the configured recovery interval, persistent
authenticated refusal ending before a test safety deadline, and retained
uncertain state. The native 20 MiB blocker and full migration/U3 failures above
